**Review: "A new green tea" (email)**

I checked each item in the draft against the brand policy and the claims rules.

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| "We've added a Japanese sencha to the shop" | Product fact (new product arriving), fine as written |
| "grassy and a little sweet" | Flavour description, a product fact |
| "best brewed cooler than you think, around 70 degrees" | Brewing guidance, fine. "Best" here is a brewing instruction, not a superlative claim about the product. |
| Numbers, ratings, testimonials, customer counts | None |
| Health, environmental or guarantee claims | None |
| Urgency or scarcity | None |
| Banned words and AI-tell structures | None. No em-dashes, exclamation points, rhetorical openers or "not just X, it's Y". |
| Voice | Warm, plain, unhurried. UK spelling. |
| Disclosure | Not needed. This is the brand's own email, with no partnership or affiliate link. |

Two optional notes, neither blocking:
- "70 degrees" could read as "70°C" so there's no doubt about the unit.
- The draft has no link to the new tea. That's a usefulness point, not a compliance one.

Per the policy, Sam (marketing lead) approves everything public, so it needs his sign-off before it goes out.
